objectives.text: Keep the Realm whole: sovereignty and territorial integrity over Greenland and the Faroe Islands, conceding American basing and security rights but not title. Copenhagen's line since January 2025 is that the island's future is decided only by Greenlanders and Danes; the 22 September 2026 trilateral defence agreement (updating the 1951 pact, with two more US Defence Areas) is presented in Copenhagen as recognising sovereignty and territorial integrity, while Trump calls it 'permanent control'.

constraints.text: Greenland is not Denmark's to trade. Under the 2009 Self-Government Act (section 21) the decision on independence belongs to the people of Greenland, with a referendum and the Folketing's consent; Prime Minister Nielsen says Greenland does not want to be owned or governed by the US; polls found 85% of Greenlanders against joining the US (January 2025). The main opposition party, Naleraq (24.5% in March 2025), wants a faster independence and closer US ties.

Every proof of loyalty (the 2023 basing agreement, the F-35s, two more US Defence Areas at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig in the 2026 deal) widens the American footprint that Trump then describes as 'permanent control'; Denmark trades military access for sovereignty on paper and may end with sovereignty that is a title without the keys.

grand_strategy.reading: Denmark is a small state whose grand strategy has been reduced, since January 2025, to one question: how to stay in the American security system while an American president claims part of its territory. The Danish answer has three layers. Keep the formal position unmovable (sovereignty over Greenland and the Faroes, self-determination for Greenlanders), pay the price in usable goods (bases, F-35s, an Arctic build-up of tens of billions of kroner), and move the quarrel into NATO and Europe, where Rutte and the European leaders can absorb it. The 22 September 2026 trilateral agreement shows the method working and its cost: the crisis is calmer, the Kingdom's flag still flies, and both sides publish opposite readings of the same text. Behind the Greenland file stands the second pillar, which is Russia: a country that sits on the Baltic's only exit, takes the hybrid blows (drones over airports, flares at a helicopter, cables) and is both one of Ukraine's leading European donors (the Kiel tracker names it, with the Netherlands, right behind Germany for May-June 2026) and a builder of a European floor under NATO. The weakness is domestic and structural: a minority coalition, a Greenland that is no longer a colony to be spoken for, and an export economy that lives on American and German markets. The grades on this card follow the structure: the United States is a reluctant ally (a treaty ally with an open grievance, not a rival), Russia a rival (not an adversary, because Denmark seeks Moscow's restraint rather than its fall), China a reluctant partner.

stances.note: NATO treaty ally since 1949, host of Pituffik and of US forces under the 2023 Defence Cooperation Agreement (approved 94-11, June 2025), buyer of 43 F-35s - and the target of Trump's claim to Greenland since December 2024 (tariff threat 6 Jan 2025, Vance at Pituffik 28 Mar 2025, envoy Landry Dec 2025, 10% tariff threat on 17 Jan 2026, invasion not ruled out until Davos on 21 Jan). Foreign Minister Rasmussen: a 'fundamental disagreement' that the two sides 'agree to disagree' on, while having said after Vance's visit (March 2025) that he 'still considers' the US a close ally. The 22 Sep 2026 trilateral agreement ends the crisis on paper but the readings differ (Trump: 'permanent control'; Frederiksen: sovereignty recognised) and Trump repeated the claim at Ankara in July. Grade follows the structure: a treaty ally under open friction, per the ontology, not a rival. Trend stable rather than warming because the deal is contested. Bond - grievance: the coercion of 2025-26 is an open wound inside the alliance.

stances.note: Copenhagen names Russia the main threat to European security (Frederiksen after the September 2025 airport drones: 'main country that poses a threat'; FE of 24 Sep 2026: limited attack on a NATO neighbour 'low but rising', more hybrid operations) and acts on it: Baltic Sentry, shadow-fleet inspections off Skagen, the DKK 70bn+ Ukraine Fund. Friction is sharp: drones over Copenhagen and Aalborg (22-25 Sep 2025, Moscow denies, calls it 'staged'), the Russian ship's flares at a Danish helicopter (14 Sep 2026; ambassador summoned, Moscow summoned the Danish ambassador-designate on 1 Oct). But Denmark's aim is Russian restraint and Ukraine's survival, not Russia's destruction or regime, so 'adversary' (mortal enemy) does not apply; the grade is our reading from the structure (rival, cooling), as the Nordic cards (SWE, FIN) grade it. Bond none: no standing tie beneath.

It used the July-December 2025 presidency to push migration (safe third country concept, return hubs) and competitiveness.
